sources.entry: Dashlane - Cloud-based password manager with award-winning design.

summary.name: Dashlane Password Manager
summary.one_liner: Dashlane is a cloud-based password manager, here marketed mainly to businesses through its Dashlane Omnix credential-security product.
use_cases: Find weak or compromised passwords across employee logins
Detect suspicious sites before employees enter credentials
Reduce IT admin time spent managing passwords
Manage and protect passwords and passkeys in one place
Get org-wide visibility into logins that SSO does not cover
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Dashlane Omnix, a credential-security product aimed at organizations. It gives org-wide visibility into logins, including those SSO misses, by detecting weak or compromised passwords. It flags password risk to employees at the point of use in the browser and detects suspicious sites before credentials are entered. The page also cites customer statistics on reduced admin time and improved employee security behavior, plus a case study of JFK Terminal 4. Specific technical details and pricing are not given on the page.
notable: Dashlane Omnix provides browser-based, point-of-use password risk alerts for employees
Detects suspicious sites before credentials are entered, beyond email filters and endpoint tools
Gives visibility into logins that SSO does not cover
Listed in awesome-mac as a cloud-based password manager with award-winning design
caveats: Pricing and plan details are not stated on the page
Page content focuses on business/enterprise use; consumer offering is not described in the text
